# Career Highlights

I have an h-index of 21, with 43 peer-reviewed papers (17 as lead
author). Twelve are in the top 10% most cited publications worldwide,
including 28 publications in the top 10% journals (e.g., Nature
Sustainability, PNAS, Current Biology). Over 85% of my publications
involve international collaboration. In the past 2 years, I have
attracted project funding of \>\$1.2 million. I collaborate frequently
with industry on applied conservation challenges; I was the Monitoring
and Data Management lead for the World Wildlife Fund's Coral Reef Rescue
Initiative and currently lead the cumulative impacts workstream of the
Blue Economy Cooperative Research Centre Marine Spatial Planning
project. I teach into five courses at Griffith, and convene two (\~140
students), with consistently high student feedback scores (\>4 out of
5). I am passionate about mentoring and science communication. I
currently supervise a post-doctoral fellow and three HDR candidates. I
am co-organising Brisbane's Soapbox Science event for National Science
Weeek and sit on the steering committee for the International Congress
of Conservation Biology to be held in Brisbane in 2025. I am well-known
for teaching R programming (\>400 trained) and Marxan decision support
tool (\>200 trained). I have \>200,000 reads in The Conversation, have been featured in general media such as live interviews on Triple J's Hack program and interviews in The Guardian, and was a semi-finalist in the FameLab science communication competition. I serve as an Early Career Representative for the School of Environment and Science and participated in Griffith's Women in Leadership program.
